newsitem.title: BURUNDI: Over 100 rebels killed in Burundi fighting - radio.
newsitem.headline: Over 100 rebels killed in Burundi fighting - radio.

text.p: Burundi state radio said on Tuesday the army killed more than 100 rebels in fighting in the south of the country on Monday.
An army spokesman, speaking earlier, said at least 26 people were killed in fighting in the same area, in Rutovu commune about 75 km (45 miles) south of the capital.
He said the dead included two civilians, four soldiers and at least 20 rebels, the spokesman added.
"We recovered 10 weapons and some ammunition and our troops counted the bodies of 20 terrorists," the spokesman said.

The army has blamed a recent spate of attacks in southern Burundi on the Forces for the Defence of Democracy, a Hutu group fighting to overthrow Burundi's Tutsi military ruler who came to power in a coup last year.

Independent sources who declined to be identified said about 300 people had been killed in an attack on a camp for displaced people in Rotovu but they refused to say the ethnic affiliation of the victims.
But the army spokesman denied this. "There's no truth to this and I have no interest in hiding it," he told Reuters.
Residents of Bururi, the nearest large town, said the rebels were now heading north across the mountains towards Gishubi, 30 km (20 miles) from Rutovu.
The aid agency International Medical Corps (IMC) evacuated its staff from southern Burundi on Sunday after heavy fighting between the army and the Hutu rebels, aid officials said.
More than 150,000 people have been killed in Burundi in massacres and civil war between the Tutsi-dominated army and rebels since the killing of Burundi's first Hutu president in 1993.
